take_homes: Run the security check as a reusable skill with two lenses (policy and agent risk). It found things I'd missed and marked my 'settled' items as 'can't tell'.
The attack is plain English in a document the agent reads, and agent output is non-deterministic, so one good result is one sample. Looking fine isn't a control.
Before wiring a new source or write access into an agent, ask whether it needs the door at all. Cutting scope beats mitigating later.

monday.move: Run the agent-audit skill against the sales-team setup I built over the weekend, and check what it can read and write before anyone uses it
monday.who: me, then our security lead for anything marked 'can't tell'
monday.when: Monday morning, before the sales team gets access
monday.stop_condition: the agent-risk report has no unmitigated high-ranked risk, or I cut the confluence access
monday.blocker: I'm not sure who will maintain the setup, and the sales team hasn't asked for it

misconception.why: The ranked risks included things my own agents already do, and 'the output looks fine' doesn't catch injection or over-broad access. I still think checking can be automated through the skill rather than done by hand every time, so it's shaken, not changed.

one_line: Skip the filler slides. The audit part is good and a bit uncomfortable, which is why it's useful, but I wouldn't repeat it for the non-engineers as is.
